items.note: Read the full article (Leipziger Zeitung, 16 Apr 2026; title matches). Confirms fee EUR 30.70 unchanged for many years, Green motion of Nov 2025, 365 EUR figure, the three stages (Mitte; 90-100%+ occupancy e.g. Plagwitz, Gohlis-Süd; Gründerzeit e.g. Schleußig, Stötteritz), MTA welcomes the extension, and first part of Langfristkonzept due before summer break 2026. Article says the administration agreed 'grundsätzlich' to a fee rise and still has to draft a new fee regulation; nothing is adopted. Overlaps with item 1 (same motion) and item 2 (365 EUR).

Motion page matches the 20 Nov 2025 original: 5% by 2030, 10% by 2035 (Gründerzeitviertel), 365 EUR from 2030, 2.3% managed (Munich 33%, Stuttgart 22%), administration proposes deferring to the Langfristkonzept before summer break 2026. But the same page now carries a 'Neufassung vom 17.06.2026' that rewords the staging (2030: five Stufe-1 areas in Mitte; 2035: rest of Mitte plus high-occupancy districts; 2040: further Gründerzeit districts) and the fee wording. The draft omits this revision. Still a proposal, not a decision. Overlaps with item 0.
items.corrected_text: The Green council group's motion of 20 November 2025 asks the mayor to expand parking management in stages: at least 5% of parking space managed by 2030 and at least 10% by 2035 (including the Gründerzeit neighbourhoods), with resident-parking fees standardised and raised gradually to 365 euro per vehicle from 2030. The motion states that only 2.3% of parking is currently publicly managed (it cites Munich 33% and Stuttgart 22%), and the administration proposed deferring specific decisions until the long-term concept for stationary traffic is presented before the 2026 summer break. The motion page also shows a revised version dated 17 June 2026 that restages the targets. This is a proposal, not a decision.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 2 Mar 2024, title matches; council meeting 28 Feb 2024) confirms fee range 10.20-30.70 under GebOSt, Greens' motion to scale resident fees by vehicle size, 365 EUR discussed, administration says no legal basis (BVerwG Freiburg ruling), Verwaltungsstandpunkt approved 32:26 with 2 abstentions, city lobbying the federal government. Only wrong detail: Weyh said that by year end there would 'probably be the first answers' to open questions on municipal discretion, not clarity.
items.corrected_text: Reported on 2 March 2024: Leipzig's resident-parking permits run from 10.20 to 30.70 euro under the national fee schedule. The Greens had asked for fees scaled by vehicle size (a rise towards about 365 euro a year was discussed), but the administration said there is no legal basis for differentiated fees, citing a Federal Administrative Court ruling against Freiburg. The council backed the administration's position by 32:26 votes with two abstentions, including lobbying the federal government for the legal basis; the city expected first answers on its room for setting fees by the end of the year.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 31 Aug 2020, title matches) confirms first new fee regulation since 2011, three zones merged to two, Zone 1 EUR 1.50 per half hour (previously 1.00 or 0.70), Zone 2 EUR 0.50 (from 0.30), 216 meters / about EUR 108,000, extra revenue about EUR 1 million if behaviour unchanged, and 'Der Stadtrat entscheidet abschließend', so correctly framed as a proposal. Very old; final adopted rates not confirmed.

Sachsen Fernsehen (title matches, 16 Apr 2026, 14:01) says the zone 'wird aufgehoben' and that the lifting 'soll im Zuge der Fortschreibung des Luftreinhalteplans umgesetzt werden', i.e. announced, with implementation tied to the plan update, not completed. The draft's 'the change is made through an update' reads as done. Other facts confirmed (since March 2011, about two-thirds of the city, only one in Saxony, limits met since 2019 at all official stations, no green sticker needed once lifted, stricter EU limits from 2030 may need new measures). Summary 'is being lifted' is acceptable; avoid 'has been lifted'.
items.corrected_text: Sachsen Fernsehen reported on 16 April 2026 that Leipzig is to lift its Umweltzone after about 15 years (in place since March 2011, covering roughly two-thirds of the city area and the only one of its kind in Saxony). The city says legal air-pollutant limits have been met at all official measuring stations since 2019; the lifting is to be implemented through the update of the Luftreinhalteplan, after which the green sticker is no longer required. The city warned that stricter EU limits from 2030 may require new measures.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 26 Mar 2025, title matches) gives 2023 SrV results: car 31.2% (36.5% in 2018), walking 32.8% (27.3%), cycling about 20% (18.7%), public transport 16.2% (17.5%), average trip length 6 to 5.3 km, 12% working fully/partly from home. Quote crediting Mobilitätsstrategie 2030 is from Thomas Dienberg, Bürgermeister for Stadtentwicklung und Bau (the draft's 'building department' is loose but acceptable). 31% car share in 2023 confirmed (31.2%). Not parking-specific.

Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 27 Apr 2024; council meeting 25 Apr 2024; title matches) confirms Fortschreibung of the Rahmenplan with measures for 2025-2028, adopted 35:20, dashboard with 231 measures worth EUR 1.3 billion, 197 in planning or construction. The 'lack of funds after years of budget cuts before 2018' is the article author's framing (backlog from the austerity phase until 2018, which Green councillor Weyh said she had not realised), not something 'councillors noted'. Only tangentially about parking; low relevance, candidate to drop.
items.corrected_text: In April 2024 (council session of 25 April) the Stadtrat approved, 35:20, the updated implementation framework (Rahmenplan) for the Mobilitätsstrategie 2030, with a concrete measures list for 2025-2028. The city's planning dashboard shows 231 measures worth 1.3 billion euro, 197 of them in planning or construction. The article attributes the funding problems to an investment backlog left by years of austerity up to 2018.

items.note: Downloaded PDF and extracted text: Neufassung VII-DS-00547-NF-01, 'Mobilitätsstrategie 2030 für Leipzig - Rahmenplan zur Umsetzung', Verwaltungsausschuss 24.06.2020, Ratsversammlung 08.07.2020 (planned, Beschlussfassung), measure list 'Stand: 22.02.2020': no. 52 improve existing P+R EUR 6.2m, no. 53 new P+R 'insb. im Süden' EUR 3.0m, no. 54 digitisation of P+R and B+R EUR 2.0m. Correctly framed as planned measures. Low parking relevance; overlaps thematically with items 8-10.

Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 9 Nov 2022, by Thomas Köhler, a former councillor, so partly opinion; title matches) confirms Stadtrat adopted the CDU motion on 11 Nov 2020 and that the administration's P+R paper was still in the Verwaltungsverfahren two years later. But the motion did not propose making P+R paid: it said it 'soll geprüft werden' whether to charge, with the ticket allowing free public transport. Item date 2020-11 refers to the council decision; the article itself is from Nov 2022.
items.corrected_text: On 11 November 2020 the Stadtrat approved a CDU motion 'Park & Ride schaffen - Umstieg auf den ÖPNV erleichtern', which called for more P+R in areas without it and asked that charging for P+R parking be examined, with the parking ticket allowing free use of public transport in Leipzig. Leipziger Zeitung (an article by former councillor Thomas Köhler) reported in November 2022 that the administration's P+R paper was still in administrative processing two years later.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 8 Oct 2023; title matches) confirms real-time free-space display in LeipzigMOVE since end of September and on leipzig.de/p+r, 814 spaces at six sites (Leipziger Messe, Knauthain, Schönauer Ring, Plovdiver Straße, Krakauer Straße, Lausen), 60 new lamp-post sensors at Knauthain and Lausen, about EUR 150,000 with 50% federal and 40% ZVNL, plan to add informal P+R areas. Omitted: the article (and its headline) says the function is currently being tested ('wird aktuell getestet'). The summary's 'digitally monitored since 2023' should say 'in a test phase since late September 2023'.
items.corrected_text: Since late September 2023 the city and LVB have been testing a real-time display of free P+R spaces in the LeipzigMOVE app and at leipzig.de/p+r, covering 814 spaces at six sites: Leipziger Messe, Knauthain, Schönauer Ring, Plovdiver Straße, Krakauer Straße and Lausen. Sixty new lamp-post sensors were installed at Knauthain and Lausen. The roughly 150,000 euro 'Park IT' project is 50% federally and 40% ZVNL funded; the city plans to later bring informal P+R areas at bus and tram stops into the system.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 13 Jan 2025; title matches): MTA says P+R S-Bahnhof Heiterblick is already in the budget from 2026; P+R Meusdorf cannot be done in 2025/26 (no available site, outside planning area, needs B-Plan with open outcome) and the administration rejects it; CDU asked for EUR 500,000 a year (250,000 per site, Heiterblick and 'Südost'); article ties P+R to RB Leipzig matches and concerts. Budgeted, not built: text does not claim completion.

Ordnungsamt notice carried by Leipziger Zeitung (25 Nov 2024; title matches): market 26 Nov-22 Dec 2024, limited city-centre parking, five P+R lots recommended (Leipziger Messe, Schönauer Ring, Plovdiver Straße, Lausen, Völkerschlachtdenkmal), served by regular LVB lines and free of charge, Augustusplatz and Goethestraße closed 26 Nov-22 Dec. Source is a city press notice republished, not editorial reporting.

Ordnungsamt notice via Leipziger Zeitung (17 Oct 2025; title matches): match 18 Oct 2025 vs Hamburger SV, P+R lots Neue Messe, Schönauer Ring, Plovdiver Straße, Völkerschlachtdenkmal, Lausen recommended; ticket gives free MDV network use five hours before and after; Ranstädter Steinweg and Jahnallee closed outbound; resident protection zone 12:30 to kick-off; Simply Red concert same evening at 20:00. All confirmed.

Downloaded PDF: Stadt Leipzig Ordnungsamt, September 2022; says city-centre garages are privately operated with prices on operators' sites and free-space counts on Park-Leit-System signs. All ten capacities quoted in the item match (1,244; 311; 554; 550; 574; 686; 820; 390; 462; 1,350). The leaflet lists an eleventh, Parkhaus Zentralstraße (75), so the draft summary's 'ten garages, about 6,900 spaces' should read eleven facilities, about 7,000 spaces (10 quoted = 6,941; 11 = 7,016). The page title is the leaflet's P+R heading; the document is mainly a stadium-event leaflet.

Page read 7 Oct 2026 (title 'Parken | Höfe am Brühl'): 820 spaces, entry 06:00-23:00 with exit via night access at any time, EUR 2.50 per commenced hour, 24h maximum EUR 18.00, evopark and card payment, charging stations including 2 Tesla. The page carries no publication or update date (only a '© 2026' footer), so it is undated live content; read 2026-10-07. Tariffs may change.

Page read 7 Oct 2026 (title 'Parken | Paunsdorf Center'): all parking free, 4,400 spaces, open 24 hours, charging: Parkplatz Mitte 1 station with 2 connectors and Eingang 3 four stations with 2 connectors each. Undated live page ('© 2026' footer only). Not on the page: 'on the eastern edge of Leipzig' and the contrast with paid central garages, which are the drafter's additions.
items.corrected_text: Paunsdorf Center, a shopping centre in Leipzig, advertises free parking everywhere on site with 4,400 spaces open 24 hours (page undated, read October 2026), plus EV charging stations (one with two connectors at the central lot and four with two connectors each at entrance 3).

items.note: Page read 7 Oct 2026 (title 'Parken – Leipzig Hbf'): Promenaden West 686 covered spaces (1 h EUR 2.00, 24 h EUR 8.00); Promenaden Ost 574 (1 h EUR 2.00, 24 h EUR 16.00); Fernbus-Terminal 550 (1 h EUR 1.50, 24 h EUR 15.00). Tariffs labelled 'Auszug'. No date on the page; undated live page, read 2026-10-07.

konii.de page redirects to the real article URL (title matches, dated 16.07.2019); only the headline and summary are readable, the full text is behind a registration paywall. Headline: 400 spaces; summary: former department-store garage becomes Tiefgarage Neumarkt, temporary option for short- and long-term parkers; APCOA PARKING appears only as a tag. Not supported by what is readable: that it 'opened on 16 July 2019' (16.07.2019 is the article date) and that APCOA runs it (APCOA's own site lists a Neumarkt garage with 412 spaces, but the Konii text does not say so). Suggest keeping only if clearly marked as headline-level.
items.corrected_text: A Konii article dated 16 July 2019 is headlined 'Tiefgarage Neumarkt eröffnet - 400 Parkplätze für Leipzigs Innenstadt'; the readable summary says the former department-store garage becomes the Tiefgarage Neumarkt, with a temporary option for short- and long-term parkers. Only the headline and summary were readable (the full text is behind registration).

items.note: Page read 7 Oct 2026 (title 'Parking in Leipzig | Q-Park'): five facilities (Am Museumswinkel, Augustusplatz/Goethestraße, Forum am Brühl, Marktgalerie, The Post); economy tariff from EUR 5 for 5 hours at Am Museumswinkel; monthly deals EUR 180 (Augustusplatz), 228 (Marktgalerie), 292 (Am Museumswinkel); online pre-booking. Undated live page ('© 1998-2026' footer only).

Page read 7 Oct 2026 (title 'Petersbogen - APCOA'): Lotterstraße 1, 554 spaces, open 24/7, from EUR 2.60 per hour, day max 08:00-22:00 EUR 10, day max EUR 20, 15 disabled spaces, 2 EV charging spaces, FLOW app for ticket- and cashless payment. Undated live page; no date visible.

Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 24 May 2025; council 21 May 2025; title matches): CDU motion for evening/weekend use of shopping-centre car parks (Düsseldorf model); the fines 'up to three digits' with camera plate capture are the CDU motion's claim, reported as such; MTA's statement welcomes it and will examine it within the Langfristkonzept; concept due second half of 2025 (it slipped later); all present councillors approved the Verwaltungsstandpunkt. The idea came from former CDU councillor Sigrun Seidel.

Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 2 Jun 2024; title matches): Stadtwerke about 640 stations/1,200 points, about 350 stations/700 points public; Goingelectric.de as of 1 May 2024 883 normal and 216 fast public points; 9,417 EVs registered; Stadtwerke tariff 53 ct/kWh normal and 63 ct/kWh fast. All confirmed. Not parking-specific; low relevance.

Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 11 May 2026; vote 29 Apr 2026; title matches): approved 52:5 with 9 abstentions, 390 bike spaces, EUR 2.178 million, city bears just under half and EUR 1.18 million is promised in 'Fördermittel'; construction to begin after the summer holidays, opening expected Q2 2027; unused car spaces are repurposed. The article does not say the grant is federal, so 'federal' is unsupported here. Bicycle parking, low relevance to car parking.
items.corrected_text: On 29 April 2026 the Stadtrat approved, 52:5 with 9 abstentions, a bicycle parking garage for 390 bikes on the east side of Leipzig Hauptbahnhof, costing about 2.178 million euro (just under half paid by the city, 1.18 million euro promised in grants). Construction is due to start after the summer holidays 2026 with opening expected in the second quarter of 2027, and car parking spaces that drivers do not use will be converted for it.

items.note: Article (Leipziger Zeitung, 27 Nov 2025; title matches): administration proposes Sunday 21 Feb 2027 for the OB election (second round 21 Mar 2027), the Stadtrat decides finally; Jung in office since 2006, aged 67 and may no longer run, term ends 28 Mar 2027. Not in the source: that this is 'under Saxon age limits' and that 'the parking and mobility agenda passes to a new mayor' (the drafter's inference). Not parking-specific: recommend dropping.
items.corrected_text: Leipziger Zeitung reported on 27 November 2025 that the city administration proposed Sunday 21 February 2027 as the date for the next Oberbürgermeister election (second round 21 March 2027), with the Stadtrat to decide finally. Burkhard Jung (SPD), in office since 2006, may not run again at 67, and his term ends on 28 March 2027.

corrected_summary: Central Leipzig garages are privately operated (operators such as Q-Park and APCOA; a September 2022 city leaflet lists eleven central facilities of about 7,000 spaces) and shown on a Park-Leit-System, while the city's own levers are on-street and resident parking. A Green council motion of November 2025 (revised in June 2026) says only 2.3% of parking is managed and proposes raising the resident fee, currently EUR 30.70 a year, gradually to EUR 365; the administration agreed in principle in April 2026 but nothing is adopted and the long-term parking concept is still pending. Park-and-ride lots are free and promoted for the Weihnachtsmarkt and RB Leipzig matches, with real-time availability tested since late September 2023 (814 spaces at six sites) and a Heiterblick lot budgeted from 2026. The city announced in April 2026 that it will lift its Umweltzone, and the 2023 mobility survey puts car trips at 31% of daily trips.
